Fix PayloadAdapter HTTP/2 reply-to-request matching

The previous code used a single pointer to track the first unreplied
request, matching replies sequentially (FIFO). This is incorrect for
HTTP/2 where responses can arrive out of order due to multiplexing.

Replace with a list of pending requests and match by stream_id for
HTTP/2 (stream_id != 0), mirroring ConnectionDescriptor's approach.

Move SOCKS5 host resolution from CaptureHelper to CaptureService

Host resolution was performed in CaptureHelper before starting the
service, but this was skipped for always-on VPN (system starts the
service directly) and BootReceiver (starts service without CaptureHelper).

Resolve the SOCKS5 proxy hostname in the capture thread using the
underlying (non-VPN) network saved before VPN establishment. This
covers all startup paths and also re-enables hostname support for
the intent-based API (disabled in 6ca1073 to work around a UI glitch
that no longer applies since resolution is now async in the service).

the packet loop starts. If resolution fails, capture is aborted.

Fix binary body corruption in HAR export

Request bodies were always decoded as UTF-8, so invalid sequences were
replaced with U+FFFD, irreversibly corrupting binary payloads. Bodies are
now base64-encoded unless they strictly decode as UTF-8, which also covers
WebSocket text frames and text bodies containing invalid sequences.

Also fix parseHeaders using the end-of-headers byte offset as a string
index, which leaked body data into the headers of non-ASCII requests.

Closes #876

Fix HAR content size for compressed responses

content.size was written from the on-wire body length, but the body is
stored decompressed, so it under-reported the size of compressed responses
(e.g. 21680 instead of 63354 bytes for a gzipped reply). It now reports the
length of the stored body, with the saved bytes in the compression field.

pcapd: make root-mode packet direction more conservative

Base the TX/RX decision on the IP layer when the capture interface IP is
known: if neither the source nor the destination matches the interface,
assume TX and don't swap the peers. This avoids misclassifying routed
traffic (e.g. when the phone acts as a hotspot) as RX just because its
destination MAC matches the interface. The MAC / SLL heuristic is now
only a fallback used when the IP layer cannot be matched (e.g. the "any"
interface, which has no single IP address).

Also keep the interface IP up to date for specific NICs, not just the
internet interface: subscribe to the IFADDR netlink groups whenever
capturing, and clear a stale IPv4 address when it can no longer be read.

See #877

pcapd: use ifinfomsg for RTM_DELLINK index

RTM_DELLINK carries a struct ifinfomsg, not ifaddrmsg. The old cast
worked only by coincidence, since ifa_index and ifi_index share the
same offset. Use the correct type to read the interface index.

Persist packet direction in root mode via pcapng EPB flags option

When capturing in root mode the direction heuristic may swap the connection
peers (tupleSwapPeers). Once dumped to a pcapng file, the IP/SLL header and
the interface info used by the heuristic are gone, so on reload the reader
defaulted every packet to TX, showing a direction inconsistent with the live
capture.

Carry the direction in the standard EPB flags option (code 2) and read it
back. This is tool-interoperable; Wireshark understands it too, showing it
as the "Point-to-Point Direction".

Also fixes a pre-existing seek desync when a comment option did not parse as
a UID.

Closes #877

Implicitly enable PCAPdroid extensions with the pcapng format

Fix crash when HTTP log export runs after fragment detaches

The TXT/HAR export in HttpLogFragment ran the file write on a background
executor while calling requireActivity()/requireContext() from the worker
thread (notably Utils.getUriStat() after the I/O completes). If the
fragment detached mid-export (rotation, navigation, activity teardown),
these threw IllegalStateException on the background thread, crashing the
app.

Capture the application Context on the UI thread before launching the
executor and use it for all content-resolver, HarWriter, getUriStat,
getString and toast calls in both dumpHttpLog() and exportHttpLogHar().

Fix leaked connections listener causing IllegalStateException

The listener was registered on capture start even when the fragment was
not resumed (e.g. offscreen ViewPager2 page), so onPause never removed
it and its callbacks ran on the detached fragment. Now it's only
registered while resumed. Same fix applied to HttpLogFragment.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Set the connections log size to the minimum (1024)
2. Open the Connections tab, then go back to the Status tab
3. Start the capture, then rotate the device
4. Generate more connections than the log size: the app crashes
